title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Umag, Croatia 2027: Guide
metaDescription: Is there all-inclusive in Umag? Hotel Aurora offers it. See what's included, prices per person vs half-board and apartments, and who it suits.
content:
## Is There an All-Inclusive Hotel in Umag?

Yes, but only one. Hotel Aurora Plava Laguna (Katoro 18, 52470 Umag) is the only all-inclusive resort in Umag itself. It is a 4-star hotel with 306 rooms on three floors with a lift, run by Plava Laguna and marketed together with Meliá. It targets families, with a pool, bikes, entertainment and two beaches. A paved beach with loungers is about 2 minutes away. A sandy beach for children is roughly 100 m from the hotel.

The hotel is on the Katoro peninsula, about 1.1 km from the Stella Maris ATP stadium and about 2.2 km from ACI Marina Umag. The Old Town is a short drive or a longer coastal walk away.

## What Is Included in All-Inclusive at Hotel Aurora?

The all-inclusive period runs from about 16 May to 8 September. The package covers:

- Buffet breakfast, 07:00–10:00
- Buffet lunch, 12:00–14:00
- Buffet dinner, 19:00–22:00
- Snacks and fast food by the pool, 10:00–18:00
- One à la carte dinner per 7 nights booked, with advance reservation. It is weather-dependent, as it is served on a sea terrace.
- Local drinks with meals and during the day

Other hotel services are charged extra. Premium spirits, imported drinks and spa services are normally not covered. Check the drinks list when booking.

## All-Inclusive Prices in Umag: Peak vs Shoulder Season

Published Aurora rates run in steps through the season:

- **Shoulder (late May, June, early September):** about €81–€110 per person per night for a standard double room with a park-side balcony. Park-side doubles start around €85 and sea-side rooms around €94.
- **Peak (July to mid-August):** about €130–€176 per person per night. The top rate is for premium sea-side rooms.
- **Single occupancy:** about €98–€184, depending on the date.

Plava Laguna Club members can get up to 10% off. Children's discounts are significant, so a family of four costs far less than four adult rates.

## All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

The figures below are rough per-person estimates for two adults in a double room. Half-board and apartment prices are typical ranges, not quotes.

| Option | Shoulder | Peak |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Aurora) | €81–110 | €130–176 |
| Half-board (Umag 3–4★) | €55–80 | €85–120 |
| Private apartment, self-catering (2 adults) | €25–45 + food €25–35 | €40–70 + food €30–45 |

All-inclusive costs about €25–50 more per person per night than half-board in peak season. That buys lunch, snacks and drinks. Self-catering in an apartment is cheapest overall, even after restaurant dinners, since local supermarkets (Konzum, Studenac, Lidl) keep daily food costs low.

## Who Should Choose All-Inclusive in Umag

- **Families with small children.** Snacks are available from 10:00 to 18:00, with no bill-splitting and no hunting for a restaurant at nap time. The shallow sandy beach is close.
- **Short stays of 3–5 nights.** There is no shopping or cooking, and arrival is easy.
- **Guests who want a set daily budget.** The cost is known in advance.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

- **Stays of a week or more.** The buffet repeats, and guest reviews describe uneven service and limited drinks selection at busy times.
- **Couples and food-focused travellers.** Istrian konobas serve fresh fish, truffle pasta and local wine at about €15–30 per main course. A buffet cannot match that.
- **Anyone who wants to explore.** Day trips to Piran, Motovun and Trieste mean paying for meals you do not eat.

The all-inclusive in Umag is a convenience product, not a gourmet one. For adults without young children, half-board or an apartment is the better choice. Eating buffet dinners in a town known for Istrian cuisine wastes the destination.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Alternatives

Hotel Savudrija, also run by Plava Laguna, is a family-oriented all-inclusive resort with about 245 accommodation units. It lies in Savudrija, the northernmost point of the Umag area, a short drive from Umag. Poreč, about 40 km south, has the widest choice of all-inclusive hotels in Istria. Check meal-plan details on each hotel's own page, because many Istrian hotels sell half-board only.

## Local Tips

- Book Aurora early for July and August. The sea-side rooms sell out first.
- Late May and September combine all-inclusive pricing with calmer beaches and sea temperatures near 20–24 °C.
- Eat one or two dinners in Umag Old Town. A quick bus or taxi ride is cheaper than a hotel upgrade.
- Outside 16 May–8 September, Aurora sells half-board or bed and breakfast, not all-inclusive.

faq.question: Does Umag have all-inclusive hotels?
faq.answer: Yes. Hotel Aurora Plava Laguna, a 4-star resort at Katoro 18, is the only all-inclusive resort in Umag. All-inclusive applies roughly from mid-May to early September.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost in Umag per person per night?
faq.answer: In shoulder season it is about €81–110 per person per night, and in peak season about €130–176 for a double room. Children's discounts and Plava Laguna Club offers of up to 10% can lower the total.

faq.question: What does all-inclusive include at Hotel Aurora?
faq.answer: It includes buffet breakfast, lunch and dinner, pool-side snacks from 10:00 to 18:00, drinks, and one à la carte dinner per 7 nights with reservation. Other hotel services are extra.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive in Umag worth it for families?
faq.answer: Yes, for families with small children and short stays, because meals, snacks and drinks are covered and a sandy kids' beach is about 100 m away. For longer stays, an apartment is usually cheaper and gives more variety.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive to Umag besides Aurora?
faq.answer: Hotel Savudrija in Savudrija, also run by Plava Laguna, is the closest alternative. Poreč, about 40 km south, has more all-inclusive hotels.
